title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
gist: Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework ('Platform') into its post-booking API (BAPI) instead of rewriting it, organizing code by business domain and enforcing boundaries with ArchUnit tests in CI. Framework-backed changes saw 64% shorter median code review time, 34% faster first substantive feedback, and directionally 29% fewer AI prompts per 100 changed lines.

insights.claim: Agoda's post-booking API (BAPI), which coordinates cancellations, amendments, refunds and customer communications, was extracted from its aging core monolith in 2019 through a largely line-by-line migration.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Illustrates how speed-to-market extractions in travel platforms accumulate structural tech debt.
insights.locator: The change addresses growing maintenance challenges

insights.claim: Merge requests on Agoda's post-booking API more than quadrupled between 2022 and 2025, while some files exceeded 4,000 lines, creating growing maintenance challenges.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Rising development throughput without boundaries raises coupling costs, a common drag on engineering productivity.
insights.quote: merge requests more than quadrupled between 2022 and 2025, while some files exceeded 4,000 lines
insights.locator: The change addresses growing maintenance challenges

insights.claim: Agoda's team framed its original monolith extraction as a deliberate tactical-over-strategic design trade-off, citing John Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design, that the business needed at the time for speed to market.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Tactical tech debt can be rational early but must be repaid incrementally as scale grows.
insights.quote: We had deliberately traded a strategic design approach for a tactical one to prioritize speed to market.

insights.claim: Rather than rewriting its post-booking API, Agoda introduced architectural boundaries incrementally through a modular monolith framework that is now the default for new modules, migrating legacy functionality opportunistically during feature work.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Incremental modular monoliths are emerging as a lower-risk alternative to microservices rewrites, reducing modernization cost.

insights.claim: Agoda's Platform framework organizes code around business domains such as cancellations, rebooking and payments rather than technical layers, with each component encapsulating logic and data access behind defined interfaces.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Package-by-component design localizes changes, a pattern relevant to enterprise modernization tooling.

insights.claim: Agoda uses ArchUnit to encode architectural constraints as automated CI tests so violations fail the build instead of relying on human reviewers, which the team calls architectural fitness functions.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Automating architectural governance in CI reduces reviewer load, a theme that becomes more valuable as AI generates more code.
insights.quote: our CI pipeline serves as an automated guardrail, catching structural drift on every pull request before a human reviewer ever sees it

insights.claim: Agoda uses the Data Mapper pattern to keep database entities and API payloads out of business logic, and typed builders to centralize object creation.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Clear separation patterns underpin the measured review-time gains.
insights.locator: Agoda uses the Data Mapper pattern

insights.claim: Spring Modulith offers a related approach to Agoda's framework, providing module verification and dependency-cycle checks for Spring Boot applications.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Modular-monolith tooling is becoming available off the shelf in mainstream Java ecosystems.

themes.theme: Measured productivity and AI usage gains

insights.claim: In Q2 2026, Agoda's framework-backed merge requests had a median review completion time of 1.08 hours versus 3.02 hours for legacy changes, a 64% reduction.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Architecture quality has a quantifiable effect on engineering throughput, supporting spend on modernization.
insights.quote: Median review completion time was 1.08 hours for framework-backed changes, compared with 3.02 hours for legacy changes.

insights.claim: At Agoda, time to first substantive review feedback was 10.34 hours for framework-backed changes versus 15.77 hours for legacy changes, about 34% shorter.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Faster feedback loops compound into delivery speed.

insights.claim: Between June and August 2026, Agoda's framework-backed changes used 29% fewer AI prompts per 100 changed lines, though median prompts per merge request were similar (20 vs. 22), and Agoda cautioned these AI findings are directional due to the short observation period.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Well-structured codebases may lower AI-assistant usage costs, implying architecture affects AI tooling ROI.
insights.quote: Agoda cautioned that the AI findings were directional due to the short observation period.
